_comment: Cold-start baseline for the CI timing gate. NOT a dev-box measurement:
regenerate it from the Startup Runner Variance workflow, never from a laptop.
A Windows dev box reads ~230ms for a bare interpreter where CI reads ~14ms,
so local numbers are off by more than any regression this gate would catch.
The tolerance is set against measured runner variance, not chosen by feel:
six independent ubuntu-latest VMs on unchanged code spread by at most 7.2%,
so 20% is ~2.8x headroom. If this gate ever flakes, raise the tolerance or
move to a same-runner A/B against the merge base - do not delete it.
Deliberately coarse. The sharp instrument for the eager-import scaling bug is
tests/unit/test_eager_imports.py, which compares module sets exactly and
cannot flake. This gate covers what that one structurally cannot see: a slow
parser build, a heavy third-party import, an algorithmic regression in
registration that adds no modules at all.

provenance.method: median of min_ms across 6 independent runner VMs, 9 timed samples each
